Cannot translate string(): no SQL CAST t: No SQL CAST TARGET spells string() on every store this adapter is executed against. TEXT and VARCHAR are both syntax errors on MySQL (ERROR 1064 on MySQL 8.4), which spells the conversion CHAR; CHAR is character(1) on PostgreSQL, where CAST(a_double AS CHAR) is '-' for -0.6 and the filter silently matches nothing. The adapter does not know its dialect by design — it renders through whichever Drizzle dialect the caller hands the query to, which is what lets one translation serve all three stores — so it cannot pick per store the way ent's WithDialect-driven render.go does. Reclassified from oracle-compared when the MySQL leg first executed the emitted cast (cerbos/query-plan-adapters#340): it was proved on SQLite and PostgreSQL only, and the numeric rendering claim had been measured against two of the three pinned images
Cannot translate string concatenation: CEL's + over strings has no dialect-independent SQL spelling: || concatenates on SQLite and PostgreSQL but is logical OR on MySQL, which spells it CONCAT(). The numeric + the adapter emits for arithmetic is silently wrong rather than a syntax error — SQLite and MySQL coerce 'prefix:' to 0, so the comparison matched nothing

Same missing dialect-independent concatenation, between two columns rather than against a constant. This adapter refuses every string `+`, so the two-column case needs no extra type information to be rejected
Cannot translate int(): SQL CAST does no: int() is required to give `%` an integer operand and has no faithful SQL lowering — CAST rounds where CEL truncates toward zero. The cast is refused before the modulo operator is reached, exactly as for cast-int-double
Unsupported value-expression operator: m: map() translates only inside hasIntersection, where the projection becomes the inner column of an EXISTS. Comparing the ordered projection itself to a literal list has no SQL form the adapter builds
Hierarchy delimiter must be a non-empty: Cerbos splits a path on an empty delimiter into one segment per character, so the relation is a strict string-prefix test; the adapter lowers descendentOf as `LIKE prefix || delimiter || '%'`, which with an empty delimiter also matches the path itself (a2, never its own descendant). The empty delimiter is refused when the hierarchy operand is parsed, before that LIKE is built
